title: Leaf Shape Detective
description: Wander through the park and discover how many different leaf shapes you can find in 20 minutes. Observe carefully — nature hides its patterns in plain sight.
steps: Choose a starting point near a cluster of trees or bushes.
Walk slowly and look at leaves on low branches and the ground.
Find at least three distinctly different leaf shapes — pointed, round, lobed.
For each shape, notice the veins and edges without picking anything.
At the end, pick a quiet spot and try to sketch the shapes from memory.
things_to_notice: How veins branch outward from the stem like tiny rivers
Whether leaves are smooth, fuzzy, or waxy to the eye
How light filters differently through thick vs. thin leaves
safety_note: Stay on marked paths. Watch your footing on uneven ground. Do not handle fallen branches.
screen_free_tip: Challenge yourself to memorise one leaf's exact shape — no photo allowed!

title: Garden Color Palette
description: Turn your garden into an art gallery! Find as many different colors as you can among flowers, stems, and soil in just 15 minutes.
steps: Walk around the garden perimeter slowly, eyes wide open.
Count how many distinct colors you can spot among plants and flowers.
Pick the three most surprising colors and remember exactly where you saw them.
Look for colors hiding in unexpected places: soil, bark edges, insect wings.
things_to_notice: Colors that appear in more than one spot — nature loves to repeat itself
How the same flower can look lighter or darker in sun vs. shade
Tiny pops of color you'd miss if you were walking fast
safety_note: Watch for low branches at eye level and uneven ground. Stay within the garden boundary.
screen_free_tip: See how many colors you can name without using your camera — use imagination instead of apps.

title: Trail Soundscape Journey
description: Put your ears in charge. Walk a short section of trail and build a mental map of every sound you hear, near and far.
steps: Stand still at the trailhead for two minutes and just listen before you move.
Walk at half your normal pace, stopping every 5 minutes to listen.
Identify at least five distinct sounds: wind, bird calls, rustling, footsteps, distant voices.
Try to figure out the direction of each sound without turning to look.
At the halfway point, stand still again for a full minute of silence.
things_to_notice: How sounds change as you move deeper into the trail
Whether the silence itself has texture — never fully quiet
The rhythm of your own breathing and footsteps
safety_note: Stay on the marked trail. Tell someone your route before you go. Stay aware of other trail users.
screen_free_tip: Leave headphones behind — your ears are your only instrument today.

title: Street Texture Safari
description: Discover how many different textures line the streets of your neighbourhood. The city is a tactile museum hiding in plain sight.
steps: Choose a block or short street loop you know well.
Look for textures on walls, fences, pavement, and tree bark — observe with your eyes.
Find at least five completely different textures and describe each in one word.
Look up — textures appear on overhead structures, ledges, and rooflines too.
Finish by ranking your top three most interesting textures.
things_to_notice: Smooth vs. rough surfaces and what causes the difference
Patterns in brickwork, pavement cracks, or weathered wood grain
How sunlight changes the appearance of the same texture
safety_note: Stay on the pavement. Follow road crossing rules. Keep aware of cyclists and vehicles.
screen_free_tip: Describe each texture to yourself in words — this builds sharper observation skills than a photo ever would.

title: Backyard Bug Watch
description: Turn your backyard into a wildlife documentary! Observe insects going about their daily lives without disturbing them.
steps: Find a patch of grass, a plant, or a log and crouch down quietly.
Stay still for two full minutes and see what moves around you.
Count how many different types of insects you can spot.
Watch one insect for a full 60 seconds — where does it go, what does it do?
things_to_notice: How insects move — do they hop, crawl, fly, or scurry?
Whether you can spot any insects carrying something
The way an insect reacts when your shadow crosses it
safety_note: Observe only — do not touch or disturb any insects or their nests. If you see a wasp or bee nest, move away calmly.
screen_free_tip: Narrate what you see out loud in a whisper — you're the nature documentary presenter today.

title: Sky Watcher's Quest
description: Lie on your back, look straight up, and discover the sky as a living, moving canvas. Clouds, birds, and light are your show.
steps: Find a clear, open grassy area in the park with a wide sky view.
Lie flat on your back on dry grass and let your eyes adjust upward.
Observe cloud shapes for five minutes — name each one as it reminds you of something.
Spot any birds in flight and watch their paths across the sky.
Track how cloud formations shift and change over 20 minutes.
In the final stretch, just rest and notice how the light changes in the sky.
things_to_notice: Whether clouds are moving fast or slowly — which way is the wind going?
How the blue of the sky deepens or fades toward the horizon
The difference between thin wispy clouds and thick puffy ones
safety_note: Choose a dry, flat spot well away from trees and footpaths. Apply sunscreen if it is sunny. Do not stare at the sun.
screen_free_tip: No photo can capture an hour of sky — let the movement live only in your memory.

title: Nature's Pattern Hunt
description: Mathematicians call it fractal geometry. You will call it amazing. Search the trail for repeating patterns hidden in plants and natural structures.
steps: Begin at the trailhead and walk slowly, eyes scanning at every level.
Look for repeating patterns: spirals in seed heads, branching in twigs, rows in bark.
Find at least four different pattern types and fix each in your memory.
Compare two different plants — can you spot a similar pattern in both?
At the halfway point, describe your favourite pattern aloud to yourself.
things_to_notice: How twig branching mirrors the shape of the whole plant
Repeating curves and spirals that appear in flowers and seed heads
Parallel lines in grass blades vs. the branching lines in a leaf
safety_note: Stay on the marked trail at all times. Do not step off the path to reach plants. Watch footing on roots and uneven surfaces.
screen_free_tip: Instead of photographing a pattern, draw it in the air with your finger — it lodges deeper in memory.

title: Bird Behaviour Observer
description: Choose one spot, sit quietly, and let the birds come to you. This quest is about patience and sharp observation, not distance covered.
steps: Find a park bench or quiet grassy spot near trees or bushes.
Sit completely still and wait two full minutes before doing anything else.
Count how many different bird calls you can hear without seeing the birds.
When you spot a bird, observe its behaviour for at least one minute.
Notice how it moves, what it reacts to, and whether other birds approach.
things_to_notice: Whether birds seem aware of you — do they face you or ignore you?
The difference in call between birds near the ground and those in the canopy
How a bird's body language changes when another bird lands nearby
safety_note: Stay seated or standing on the path — do not approach birds or move toward them. Maintain a respectful distance.
screen_free_tip: Count bird calls on your fingers instead of recording them — your ears are more reliable than you think.
